research_goal: Create level-based MMA teaching, assessment, unlock, hold, and regression logic for SFTC. The model treats MMA level as domain-specific: a user may be intermediate in striking but beginner in wrestling, grappling, or contact readiness.

source_refs.title: Unified MMA Rules
source_refs.notes: Used for rules, scoring, and safety context.

source_refs.title: IMMAF Rules Document
source_refs.notes: Used for amateur progression and competition safety context.

technical_principles.summary: MMA level should not be a single permanent label. A user can be intermediate in boxing, beginner in cage wrestling, and beginner in submission defense. Retrieval should unlock work by domain readiness.
Contact intensity is earned through stance, guard, defense, safe falling, tap culture, symptom reporting, and coach/user readiness evidence.

MMA should progress from solo mechanics, to cooperative partner work, to constrained resistance, to controlled sparring, to open sparring or camp-specific work. Hard intensity should not arrive before technical control.

beginner.definition: Learning safe movement, basic striking, basic wrestling, positional awareness, partner safety, and low-contact skill practice.

intermediate.definition: Connecting phases with controlled partner resistance and managing technical quality under fatigue.
locked: hard fight simulation without recovery tracking
advanced submission intensity without escape competence

advanced.definition: Opponent- and phase-specific planning with contact/load periodization, tactical adaptation, and fight-camp structure.

common_errors: treating boxing level as MMA level
unlocking sparring before defense and symptom reporting
using exhaustion to teach technical skills
ignoring grappling readiness because striking looks good
progressing contact intensity without tracking symptoms and recovery
safety_constraints: No contact escalation with head symptoms.
No advanced submissions without tap culture and escape education.
No fight-camp conditioning before base fitness and skill control.
Return-to-contact must be staged and conservative.

sport_training_rules.rule: MMA level should be assessed by domain: striking, wrestling, cage control, ground control, submissions, sparring/contact, S&C, and fight IQ.
recommended_action: Use the weakest safety-relevant domain to gate contact and advanced drills.
Allow strength work and non-contact skill to progress even when contact is held.
blocked_action: Do not assume an athlete is advanced in MMA because they are advanced in one component art.

planning_rules.rule: Select MMA drills by the athlete's readiness in the specific domain, not by global experience alone.
recommended_action: Use beginner grappling progressions for a strong striker with weak wrestling.
Use non-contact technical work when contact readiness is not proven.
blocked_action: Do not unlock hard sparring, cage wrestling, or advanced submissions from a general intermediate label alone.

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build safe MMA foundations across striking, wrestling, ground awareness, partner safety, and physical base.
Connect MMA phases under controlled resistance while managing contact and fatigue.

skill_assessments.summary: Assesses MMA readiness by domain instead of a single global label.

minimum_evidence: no worsening head, neck, shoulder, wrist, back, hip, knee, or ankle symptoms
basic stance, guard, sprawl, technical stand-up, and tap culture are reliable
completion and RPE trends are inside target range
promote_when: can execute simple MMA actions under light partner input
hold_when: unsafe falling, tapping, or contact behavior
skill quality collapses under low fatigue
level_transition_rules.backend_action: Unlock controlled partner resistance, positional sparring, and phase-connection drills while keeping hard sparring gated.

minimum_evidence: 8+ additional weeks or 16+ completed MMA/S&C sessions
controlled sparring and grappling history without symptom escalation
can connect striking, wrestling, cage, and ground phases
contact load and recovery are tracked
promote_when: can adjust tactics by score, time, and opponent reaction
hold_when: head, neck, hand, shoulder, rib, back, knee, or ankle symptoms are unresolved
advanced work creates sloppy defense or poor recovery
level_transition_rules.backend_action: Unlock advanced fight-camp, opponent-specific, and round-simulation planning only with readiness and contact-load controls.
